guides.title: Near Eastern, Abrahamic & European Origin Stories: Atrahasis, Genesis & Qur'anic Creation, Bundahishn, Hesiod & the Eddas
guides.description: Creation traditions from Sumerian–Babylonian cuneiform tablets, Jewish, Christian and Islamic scriptures (Genesis and Qur'an), Zoroastrian Bundahishn, Greek Hesiod/Prometheus and Norse Eddas.
guides.intro: Across the ancient Near East, Iranian plateau, and Mediterranean–Nordic Europe, foundational literary and scriptural traditions explore human origins through earth/clay fashioned by divine craft, moral breath infused into mortal bodies, primal cosmic order wrestled out of chaos, and world-renewal across generations.
guides.scope: Primary sacred and classical literary traditions across Sumer and Babylon, Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Zoroastrianism, Archaic Greece, and Medieval Scandinavia.

points.label: Mecca & Medina (Qur'anic Creation)

points.label: Boeotia & Athens (Hesiod's Theogony / Works & Days)
points.description: Chaos -> Gaia/Uranus/Cronus -> Zeus; Five Ages (Gold through Iron), Deucalion's thrown stones, and Prometheus molding mortals from wet earth.

points.description: Ginnungagap fire-meets-ice chasm, Ymir fashioned into world, and Odin, Vili, and Vé carving Ask and Embla from coastal driftwood.

sections.heading: 1. Mesopotamian Cuneiform Accounts: Eridu Genesis, Enki & Ninmah, Atrahasis & Enuma Elish

paragraphs.text: Excavated cuneiform libraries from Nippur, Sippar, Babylon, and Nineveh preserve the oldest written human origin narratives in Sumerian and Akkadian. In the *Song of the Hoe* and *Enki and Ninmah*, humanity sprouts out of dark earth broken open by Enlil's cosmic hoe (*al*) or is hand-shaped out of sweet subterranean **Abzu clay** by birth goddesses **Namma** and **Ninmah** while **Enki** designs diverse human forms and assigns every person—including elders and people with disabilities—meaningful social roles inside temple and city life.

In the 17th-century BCE Old Babylonian epic **Atrahasis**, junior working gods rebelled against digging the Tigris–Euphrates canals for elder deities—prompting Enki and womb-goddess **Bēlet-ilī / Mami** to mix clay with the flesh, blood, and intellectual planning-spirit (*ṭēmu*) of slain rebel god **Wê-ila (Ilawela)**, creating seven human male and female pairs from fourteen pinched clay lumps to bear cosmic labor, later nearly wiped out by Enlil's Flood before hero **Atrahasis** survived in a pitched reed-boat. Later Babylonian **Enuma Elish** narrated **Marduk** splitting sea-dragon **Tiamat**'s corpse to vault heavens over earth and shaping humanity (*lullû*) from defeated **Qingu**'s blood.

sections.heading: 2. Abrahamic Traditions: Jewish, Christian & Islamic Creation (Genesis 1–2 & Qur'anic Creation of Adam)

paragraphs.text: Inside Jewish and Christian scripture, **Genesis 1** breaks radically with battling sky monsters: one transcendent Creator speaks light, firmament, dry land, stars, sea creatures, and animals effortlessly out of primordial chaos (*tohu wa-bohu*), crowning Day Six by creating **humanity—both male and female—in the Divine Image (*Imago Dei* / *Tzelem Elohim*)** as equal bearers of dignity and stewardship before resting on the Sabbath. Immediately beside it, **Genesis 2** weaves an earthy, intimate garden story: God stoops like a potter to shape *ʾādām* (human) from fertile red humus (*ʾădāmâ*), breathes life-breath (*nishmat chayyim*) into his nostrils, and builds **Eve (*Ḥawwāh*)** directly from Adam's own bone-and-side (*tsela*) as *ezer kenegdo*—an equal facing partner.

Across multiple **Qur'anic Surahs** (notably *al-Baqarah* 2:30–38, *al-Ḥijr* 15:26–33, *Ṣād* 38:71–76, and *al-Nisāʾ* 4:1), **Islam** teaches that **Allah** declared to the angels the appointment of humanity as moral trustee/vicegerent (**Khalīfah**) on Earth. Gathering diverse colors of dust and clay (*turāb*, malleable *ṭīn*, ringing fired pottery *ṣalṣāl*), God fashioned **Ādam** cleanly with divine hands, breathed His Spirit (**Rūḥ**) inside him, taught Ādam the comprehensive **Names of All Things** surpassing angelic knowledge, created his mate (**Ḥawwāʾ**) from a single shared soul (*nafs wāḥidah*), and commanded every angel to bow in honor before human dignity—with only proud jinn **Iblīs** refusing, defining Adam and Hawwa's descent from the Garden not as an inherited taint of original sin, but as the beginning of sincere repentance (*tawbah*), forgiveness, and Earthly moral choice.

sections.heading: 3. Zoroastrian Bundahishn, Archaic Greek (Hesiod & Prometheus) & Norse Eddas (Ask & Embla)

paragraphs.text: In the Zoroastrian Middle Persian **Bundahishn** ('Primal Creation'), **Ahura Mazda** constructed the world in seven luminous spiritual-and-material stages—stone sky, water, flat earth, single prototypical plant, Primordial White Ox (*Gāv ī Ēwdād*), radiant mortal ancestor **Gayōmard**, and pure fire—before dark antagonist **Angra Mainyu (Ahriman)** pierced through from below to stain existence with death. Out of Gayōmard's buried seed sprang a twin-stemmed green **rhubarb (*rīvās*) plant** after forty years, splitting into **Mashya and Mashyana**, the first mortal pair whose ethical alignment (*good thoughts, good words, good deeds*) aids Ahura Mazda in ultimately renewing Creation (*Frashokereti*).

In Archaic Greece, **Hesiod** (*Theogony* & *Works and Days*, c. 700 BCE) opened from yawning **Chaos** yielding **Gaia (Earth)**, Tartarus, and Eros; Gaia bore starry Sky (**Uranus**), whose overthrow by **Cronus** and later **Zeus** ushered in **Five Ages of Mortals** (Golden people living effortlessly like gods, Silver, violent Bronze, noble Heroes at Thebes/Troy, and hard Iron), while later **Ovid** and Greek tragedians celebrated Titan **Prometheus** molding mortals from rainwater-moistened earth and stealing hidden fennel-stalk fire, complemented by flood survivors **Deucalion & Pyrrha** casting Gaia's 'bones' (stones) behind them. North across medieval Iceland and Scandinavia, Old Norse **Völuspá** and Snorri Sturluson's **Prose Edda** picture icy **Niflheim** and fiery **Muspelheim** clashing inside empty yawn **Ginnungagap**, melting frost giant **Ymir** and nourisher cow **Auðumbla**—whose bones Odin, Vili, and Vé built into mountains, skull into heavens, and blood into seas before discovering two lifeless sea-tossed **driftwood logs** (ash & elm / vine) along the shore and breathing soul, wit, warm blood, and speech into **Ask and Embla**.
